statement: Under P-IISS and RTVC the regret bound has only polynomial (not exponential) dependence on H w.r.t. eps_q.
source: arXiv:2603.20538, Section 3.1-3.2 (Theorem 3, Def 3 P-IISS, Def 4 RTVC)

dynamical_instantiation.setup: 1-D contractive expert u*(x)=Lu*x, x_{h+1}=a x_h+u_h, a+Lu=0.1; Lipschitz learner gain a+Lu+beta=1.1>1
dynamical_instantiation.interpretation: RTVC (binning) capped error -> O(H*eps_q) polynomial; Lipschitz (Wasserstein) uncapped error -> exp(H) compounding (growth rate 1.133 per step), exactly the paper's Remark after Def 4.

mutation_test.name: toggle deployed-policy continuity RTVC (thresholded) -> Lipschitz (Wasserstein)
mutation_test.effect: RTVC gives O(H*eps_q) polynomial regret (log-fit slope ~0); Lipschitz (non-RTVC) gives exp(H) regret (growth rate 1.133>1 per step). Dropping RTVC breaks the 'polynomial not exponential' property -> claim attributable to RTVC.

notes: Verified = the Theorem-3 bound under RTVC is polynomial in H (slope 1 in loglog) with linear eps_q dependence, and a faithful 1-D instantiation shows the contrast: RTVC (thresholded) continuity yields O(H*eps_q) regret while Lipschitz/Wasserstein (non-RTVC) continuity yields exponential regret. The mutation (drop RTVC) flips the regret from polynomial to exponential, confirming the claim.
